text.p: Programme of soccer matches in the German first division this weekend.

Rostock, only east German side in the Bundesliga, aim to continue their climb away from relegation zone but up against an in-form Bochum side who beat them 1-0 in first half of the season and want points in their campaign for a UEFA Cup place.
Home side in deep relegation trouble after being on the wrong end of a 5-0 thrashing by Bayern last weekend. Bielefeld without suspended midfielder Guenther Schaefer.

Stuttgart striker Fredi Bobic, the Bundesliga's leading scorer, unlikely to play after sustaining a head injury in Germany's World Cup qualifier against Ukraine on Wednesday. St Pauli fighting against the drop but will take heart from the fact they beat Stuttgart 2-1 earlier in the season.

This northern clash has been finely-balanced over the years -- Hamburg have won 21 times, Bremen 20 times and the sides have drawn on 24 occasions. Bremen still harbouring hopes of a UEFA Cup place while Hamburg still need points to remain clear of relegation dogfight.

Karlsruhe unsettled by speculation that striker Sean Dundee will leave the club at the end of the season. Team also suffering from Dundee's loss of form. Cologne stopped run of defeats with draw against Schalke last weekend and will hope to continue revival in front of a home crowd.

Ruhr Valley derby features Germany's two European finalists this season. Schlake boosted by news striker Martin Max has resumed training after injury layoff. He's unlikely to feature against Dortmund but should be fit for next week's UEFA Cup final first leg against Internazionale of Milan.
Doomed Freiburg only playing for pride against mid-table Duisburg, who look to have done enough to avoid going straight back down to the second division.

Leverkusen have chance to draw level on points with leaders Bayern if they can beat Moenchengladbach. The home side may have a major say in who wins the title, even though they are in mid-table, as they face Bayern on the last day of the season.

Munich derby promises to be passionate affair, with both sides playing for pride and vital points. Bayern need them for their championship campaign while 1860 want a UEFA Cup berth. Question mark hangs over Bayern midfielder Mario Basler, who sustained thigh injury against Ukraine.
